title: Unknown-tail stochastic nonconvex stationarity with known smoothness and initial gap
summary: A common algorithm adapts to an unknown moment exponent and noise scale when population smoothness and initial-gap budgets are known.

description_paragraphs: Construct one budget-indexed algorithm family for smooth nonconvex stationarity that adapts to an unknown centered-noise moment exponent.
task.formulation: Construct one budget-indexed algorithm family for smooth nonconvex stationarity that adapts to an unknown centered-noise moment exponent.

description_paragraphs: The differentiable lower-bounded $F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $F(x_0)-\inf F\le\Delta$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla F)\le L$. The positive budgets $L,\Delta$, initial point and finite dimension are public. For some fixed $p\in(1,2]$ and $\sigma\ge0$, the oracle noise has centered conditional pth moment at most $\sigma^p$. Neither p nor sigma is supplied to the algorithm.

assumptions.description: The differentiable lower-bounded $F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $F(x_0)-\inf F\le\Delta$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla F)\le L$. The positive budgets $L,\Delta$, initial point and finite dimension are public. For some fixed $p\in(1,2]$ and $\sigma\ge0$, the oracle noise has centered conditional pth moment at most $\sigma^p$. Neither p nor sigma is supplied to the algorithm.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

description_paragraphs: A query at a history-measurable point returns only a full vector $g_t$ with $\mathbb E[g_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=\nabla F(x_t)$ and $\mathbb E[\|g_t-\nabla F(x_t)\|_2^p\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le\sigma^p$. The conditional law may depend on the history. No function value, repeated evaluation of one sample at different points, or sample-gradient smoothness is available.

description_paragraphs: The risk is $\mathcal R_T^{\mathsf A}(p;L,\Delta,\sigma)=\sup_{d,I,\mathcal O}\mathbb E\|\nabla F(\widehat x_T)\|_2$, with one common family $\mathsf A=(\mathsf A_T)$ required to apply for every fixed p. Constants in the analyzed risk may depend on p; the algorithm does not.

description_paragraphs: T is a public deterministic cap on every path. Training, candidate generation, validation and selection calls all count. Pointwise inversion of a risk bound at a specified p is an analysis quantity and does not furnish a stopping rule that knows p.

description_paragraphs: Queries, stopping decisions and outputs are arbitrary measurable functions of the observed history and public inputs. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Internal exact-real computation and storage are uncharged.
A private random seed independent of the fixed instance is permitted.
The complete algorithm family is the same for all p and sigma. Known smoothness and gap budgets may enter its step sizes; unknown tail and noise scales may not.

$$
\mathcal R_T^{\mathsf A}(p;L,\Delta,\sigma)=\sup_{d,I,\mathcal O}\mathbb E\|\nabla F(\widehat x_T)\|_2
$$

Choose one common family with inputs only T,L,Delta,x0 and d. For every fixed p, evaluate its risk uniformly over the corresponding instance and oracle class. The family may not encode a p-dependent tuning choice.
